claim: BIS's Proposed Charging Letter against Cadence alleged 61 EAR violations: 56 unlicensed exports/loans to CSCC (an NUDT alias) from about September 2015 to September 2020, two charges for the actual and attempted transfer of those items to Phytium (Nov 2020-Feb 2021), and three charges for EDA software downloads by Entity-Listed Mikron, Huawei and SMIC between September 2016 and December 2021.
evidence: "...a Proposed Charging Letter to Respondent that alleges that Respondent committed 61 violations of the Regulations." (Order p.1); Charges 1-56 (CSCC), Charge 57 (transfer to Phytium), Charge 58 (attempted hardware transfer), "Charges 59-61 ... Mikron ..., Huawei ..., and ... SMIC ... to continue making downloads" (pp.4-7)

metric.name: EAR violations alleged and admitted (Cadence BIS settlement)
metric.population: Charges in BIS Proposed Charging Letter admitted by Cadence

notes: Resolves CON-0050: the BIS press release itemised only the 56 CSCC + 2 Phytium charges; the 3 download charges make 61.

claim: Kirkland & Ellis wrote in June 2025 that BIS's May 2025 EDA restrictions were communicated by letters to three major EDA companies and appeared to take the form of a traditional 'is informed' letter, used in a novel way to name China as a whole rather than specific entities.
evidence: "BIS ... reportedly communicated broad new restrictions on the export of electronic design automation (EDA) software to China via letters to three major EDA companies."; "The outreach appears to take the form of a traditional BIS 'is informed' letter"; "...listing China itself as an unacceptable diversion risk" (Kirkland Alert, 30 Jun 2025, p.1)

claim: A Federal Register search found no BIS document mentioning 'electronic design automation' published between 1 May and 31 August 2025, consistent with the May 2025 EDA licence requirement not having been published as a rule.
evidence: Federal Register API query (term "electronic design automation", agency industry-and-security-bureau, publication date 2025-05-01 to 2025-08-31) returned: "count":0
notes: Searched on 2026-10-01. Absence in the Federal Register does not exclude non-public BIS letters, which is the point.
